function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
CPU usage refers to the amount of processing power that your computer’s central processing unit (CPU) is currently consuming. It’s usually expressed as a percentage of the total available capacity. A high CPU usage (e.g., above 80–90 %) can indicate that one or more processes are demanding a lot of resources, which may lead to slower performance or overheating.

If you want to see real‑time CPU usage on a Windows machine, you can open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc) and look at the “CPU” column under the Processes tab. For a quick command‑line check, you can run:

```cmd
wmic cpu get loadpercentage
```

This will return the current overall CPU load as a single number. If you’d like me to execute that command right now, just let me know!
